car.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production sprite for a top-down pixel-art arcade snake game, displayed in an 80 by 80 game-pixel square.
Primary request: one sporty compact car seen straight from overhead, pointing RIGHT (front bumper and headlights on the RIGHT, rear bumper on the LEFT). Adult arcade visual style, punchy and immediately readable.
Scene/backdrop: completely transparent alpha background, no road, no ground, no cast shadow outside the sprite.
Subject: one red compact car with a dark navy outline, light icy-blue windshield and rear window, four small dark tires, pale headlights on the right and tiny red-orange rear lights on the left. Clearly separated hood, roof and rear. No driver visible.
Style/medium: authentic simple low-resolution pixel art, as if drawn on a 32 by 32 pixel grid and enlarged with nearest-neighbor. Hard square pixel blocks, flat restrained shading, thick dark silhouette, no smooth vector curves or antialiasing, no 3D perspective.
Composition/framing: square canvas 1024 by 1024. Exactly one centered horizontal car, car occupies about 80 percent of canvas width and 52 percent of canvas height. Even transparent padding. Car's center exactly at canvas center. Orthographic top down, zero angle, right-facing.
Constraints: no text, no letters, no logos, no watermark, no extra objects or effects. Genuine transparency. This is the final game texture, not a sprite-sheet preview or mockup.
refinements:
Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: transparent top-down player car sprite for an arcade game.
Edit target: the supplied red car sprite. Simplify it to a clearly readable Commodore 64-inspired sprite, with MUCH FEWER details and large flat pixel clusters. Preserve EXACT original square canvas, centered car silhouette, its length and width, transparent padding, wheel and mirror locations. Front must still point RIGHT. The whole square canvas is displayed at 80x80 game pixels; actual car is about 74x36 pixels.
Draw as if designed on a 40x40 logical pixel grid: about 37 pixels long and 18 pixels wide, with crisp staircase edges and broad flat areas. Do not reduce the car's physical footprint.
Use only 6 or 7 solid retro colors: dark navy outline/wheels, muted brick red body, one lighter red highlight, one darker red shadow, cyan glass, pale cyan windshield highlight, pale yellow headlamps. C64-inspired muted red #9A6759 with body shadow #68372B; glass #70A4B2. Make the car clearly red, with a simple roof, one simple windshield and one rear window. At most ONE small highlight per glass panel.
REMOVE fine door seams, glossy reflections, fine side windows, multiple bevels, tire tread, gradients and tiny trim. Flat roof and hood, simple rectangular wheels. Selective large color clusters, no all-over dithering. The result should feel like an 8-bit car rather than a detailed modern pixel-art car.
Exactly one vehicle. TRUE transparent alpha outside its silhouette. No shadow, road, labels, logos, lighting halo, border, other objects or presentation sheet.
car.usage: Simplified C64-inspired player car with large color blocks, sparse highlights and the original footprint. Runtime scales the transparent square texture to 80x80.

storefront.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production background storefront strip for a top-down pixel-art parking-lot game.
Primary request: a very WIDE, LOW storefront facade of a small shop selling alcohol and snacks. Entire image is the facade, seen straight-on in classic top-down RPG convention. No ground or parking lot.
Canvas panoramic 3072x384 (8:1 aspect ratio) if possible. Facade will be displayed at 1280x160 pixels across the TOP of the game board. Keep all important design in the LOWER two thirds of image: the upper third must be simple flat dark navy fascia so score and pause HUD can overlay it.
Lower two-thirds: long warm lit shop window divided by neat dark frames, rows of small amber/green beer and wine bottles plus colorful crisp/chip bags and packaged snacks on shelves, a closed double glass entrance at center. Thin cream masonry frame and low light-gray sill. Recognizably an alcohol and snack store. Small burgundy sign strip centered above windows with ONLY exact text "ALKOHOL I PRZEKASKI" in bold cream block letters, positioned beneath the empty top HUD band. No brand names, logos or extra text.
Style: crisp chunky 2D pixel art matching a top-down arcade game, navy outlines, warm cream illumination, amber glass, restrained burgundy and teal details, simple flat shaded rectangular pixels. Pixel grid as though image was 320x40 pixels then enlarged nearest neighbor. No photorealism, no perspective recession, no isometric roof, no angled walls. Orthographic straight facade, no large building roof.
Composition: facade touches left and right image edges, no margins, no sky, no transparent background, no people, no cars, no trees. All opaque background. One continuous storefront from edge to edge, horizontally symmetrical composition about central doors. Leave top third calm and dark.

fenceCorner.prompt:

Generate exactly ONE square corner tile, not a sheet. Genuine transparent alpha background, no asphalt. Same gray/silver steel, navy outline, diamond chain-link mesh and pixel density as reference. No scene, no text, no margin.
EXACT geometry as fractions of this square:
- A vertical fence approaches from TOP EDGE at x=50% and runs down to the tile CENTER (50%,50%). It occupies x=43%..57%.
- At the center it joins a horizontal fence going RIGHT, continuing all the way through the RIGHT EDGE at y=50%. This horizontal band occupies y=38%..62%.
- The two fences are firmly connected at the bend with ONE square steel corner post and visible metal angle bracket. No gap. The result is an L shape like the glyph └, TOP to RIGHT only.
- Neither leg continues below or to the left of the center. No fence along bottom edge or left edge.
- Transparent everywhere outside the L silhouette, including every diamond mesh hole.
- Fence legs MUST extend flush to top and right canvas edges to join adjacent tiles.
- The corner post is centered EXACTLY (50%,50%) with a visible silver right-angle bracket joining the two metal rails.
- Draw absolutely square-on in flat 2D arcade convention, NOT isometric, NOT perspective.
- At display size80x80 the vertical leg is about11pixels wide, horizontal leg about19pixels tall. Preserve those proportions rather than making both legs thick.
Constraints: single crisp pixel-art tile, square canvas1024x1024. Match the reference's steel fence only, no plants, ground, shadow, cars or extra posts away from the L. No antialiasing or soft shadows. Authentic transparency.
fenceCorner.usage: Only the bolted bracket region (544, 510, 205, 245) is used. Fence legs are drawn from parking-atlas tiles 10 and 12 to preserve matching rail spacing and mesh.
